title: Regional road, bridge and transit decisions, plus long-term care grant referral
subtitle: Library transfer study, disability benefit and Toronto-style funding advocacy, lobbyist registry, bike lane opposition, veterans transit pass review
overview: Regional Council approved a package of transportation measures, including an all-way stop at Fischer-Hallman and Roseville roads, a lower speed limit on part of Weber Street in Waterloo, preferred designs for six road corridors, and an accelerated pedestrian bridge over the Conestogo River on the Kissing Bridge Trailway {{vote:m8}}. Council also started the process of taking over three road segments from Wilmot Township, with up to $200,000 for safety work at the Punkeydoodles intersection {{vote:m9}}.

Council referred a request from Tri-County Mennonite Homes for a development charge grant to the December 11 budget committee, with staff to report on how it could be funded {{vote:m5}}. It asked staff to study transferring library branches to the townships {{vote:m6}}, approved a lobbyist registry by-law and code of conduct {{vote:m11}}, and called for provincial action on disability support rates {{vote:m7}}.

Council opposed proposed provincial rules on bike lanes {{vote:m14}}, asked the province for a funding deal like those given to Toronto and Ottawa {{vote:m10}}, and directed a review of the veterans transit pass as part of the GRT business plan {{vote:m15}}. Staff were also asked to update Council on the Anti-Racism Advisory Working Group recommendations. After a closed session on Jack Young Civic Award nominations, the minutes record no public decision.

decisions.item: Transportation and Kissing Bridge Trailway bridge
decisions.detail: Council approved an all-way stop at Fischer-Hallman and Roseville roads, a 50 km/h limit on part of Weber Street, preferred corridor designs, and an accelerated Conestogo River pedestrian bridge with a new two-year project manager position.
Council began the process to transfer three Wilmot road segments to the Region and approved an upset limit of $200,000 for safety improvements at the Punkeydoodles intersection.
Council referred the development charge grant request to the December 11 budget committee, with further information on how the exemption could be achieved.
Council directed staff to report on the costs and benefits of transferring Regional library branches to the townships, consulting township staff.
Council approved the lobbyist registry by-law and code of conduct, received the 2024 third quarter update, and amended the capital budget and forecast.
Council opposed proposed provincial approval requirements for bike lanes that remove traffic lanes and called on the province to withdraw the legislation.
Council asked, through the Regional Chair's office, that the five area MPPs seek a fair funding deal comparable to those reached with Toronto and Ottawa.
Council directed a review of the veterans GRT pass, including spouses, widows and widowers, within the current GRT business plan, with cost estimates.

debate: On the Tri-County Mennonite Homes request, the delegate said the home is non-profit, faces a development charge cost for the expansion, and cannot recover it as municipally owned or for-profit homes can. The delegate noted other municipalities waive such charges for non-profit long-term care.

Staff said long-term care homes do not qualify for an exemption under the current by-law and none was granted in the past ten years. Any grant would need matching funds in the development charge reserve, and Council recently decided new grants should go through a defined process.

One councillor worried that granting the request would set a precedent, since the Region would still have to provide the servicing and pay the cost from other sources. Supporters of the referral saw long-term care as housing for seniors and wanted the debate left for budget day.

A delegate from the former Anti-Racism Advisory Working Group argued that the Community Safety and Well-Being Plan is no substitute for an anti-racism plan, and asked for a report on the group's recommendations. Council asked staff for an update.

In support of the bike lane motion, the mover argued the provincial rules overreach into local jurisdiction, would delay infrastructure, and would reduce safety for cyclists. Delegates on water and land use raised concerns about aggregate extraction near Regional wells and the Wilmot land assembly; Council did not debate these.
